messages:
deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy: migration/2026_03_add_user_flags at 02:00 UTC (change window). Running preflight checks: schema diff, long-query scan, index availability. Canaries: 3.
maya: heads-up — this migration backfills a flag across ~1.2B rows. we need a plan to avoid table-level locks.
kevin: propose: ADD COLUMN new_flag boolean NULL; background backfill via replica -> apply in batches; then follow up with atomic swap using trigger + small cutover. avoids full-table lock.
anita: agreed. doced rollback too? if we need to revert mid-backfill we must ensure apps can read either column. recommend feature flag read fallback.
maya: i'm worried about read replica lag during backfill. can we run backfill on a replica and then stream changes via logical replication?
kevin: yes — plan: 1) add column on primary (fast, metadata only), 2) start background worker on replica that updates in chunks: `pgbench -f backfill.sql -c 1 -T 3600` with batching by id ranges, 3) set up logical decode slot to capture changes during backfill and apply to replica copy, 4) once caught up, flip reads to new column via feature flag.
anita: rollback script staged: `infra/db/migrations/202603_add_user_flags/down.sql` which is basically `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS new_flag;` — but note: dropping will lose any collected data. we should only run if we decide to abort and accept data loss.
maya: safe rollback alternative: disable writes to new_flag via app feature flag and stop backfill jobs; keep column and leave for re-run. prefer that over drop.
srebot: monitoring rule created: alert if single migration query > 5m or if replica_lag > 30s during backfill.
deploy-bot: preflight results: schema diff OK, no blocking locks detected, canary cluster tests passed (3/3).
maya: rollout policy: staged batches 10% -> 30% -> 100% with 15m observation windows. abort criteria: >5% 5xx, >1s p95 latency regression, replica_lag > 30s sustained.
kevin: I'll be oncall for the window. I also pushed a small compatibility shim to client pinned at `client-sdk@1.3.2` to read both `user_flags` and `new_flag` until cutover.
anita: release notes snippet ready: "DB migration: add new user_flag column (background backfill). Apps pinned to client-sdk@1.3.2 for read fallback. Rollback: stop backfill jobs + disable writes; full drop only by exec. See infra/db/migrations/202603_add_user_flags for scripts."
maya: when do we want the short manual checkpoint? plan a dry-run tonight in staging at 23:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: Dry-run scheduled: staging 23:00 UTC; production 02:00 UTC. I will post updates and can abort if any gating rule fires.
kevin: awesome. if abort needed, run:```bash
# stop backfill
kubectl -n batch delete job user-flag-backfill-*
# disable writes in feature flag
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN' https://flags.internal/disable/new_flag
# monitor replica/promote port
```
anita: noted. I'll keep `down.sql` and the migration logs linked in the PR.
maya: thanks everyone — i'll run the staging dry-run and report back. :thumbsup:
